parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks national and state exposures. Nationally: binary sex definition, passport/visa marker restrictions upheld Nov 2025, an entry cable telling officers to refuse cases where documents cast doubt on sex and to consider lifetime fraud ineligibility, with documented stranded travellers and eight foreign governments issuing advisories — a universal entry/document exposure. The state adds its own layer: K-12 facility bans (2022, 2025), a 2023 executive order restricting all state facilities including shelters and incarceration by birth sex, foreclosed marker changes, an adult public-facility/funding care ban (SB 904, misdemeanour for providers), and no state discrimination or hate-crime coverage. Mitigations are real but partial: functioning courts, national hate-crime and employment protections, emergency-care carve-out, no criminalisation of trans identity. Combined: tier-1 institutional exposures without imprisonment likelihood.

entry_documents.exposure: Executive order bars self-selected gender on passports/visas; X markers ended Feb 2025; Nov 2025 Supreme Court allowed restrictions. Entry cable orders refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and directs consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility. Travellers report confiscated/blocked passports and stranding; eight governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements, has limited waivers, is never automatic. Existing X passports valid to expiry. ACLU suit pending; legal-aid FAQ guides document strategy.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal or fraud finding can cascade into detention, state custody placement by birth sex under the 2023 order, and care denial under SB 904.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for transgender inmates from 2026 (hair, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs); reporting of trans prisoner numbers stopped 2025. Immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse. 2023 state order applies birth-sex rules to incarceration.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; courts have enjoined several orders. No trans-specific criminal offence for presentation documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any state arrest (e.g. facility trespass analogues elsewhere) routes into a custody system with documented hostile practices.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State: K-12 bans (2022 SB 615, 2025) plus Aug 2023 executive order applying birth-sex definitions to all state buildings, shelters, crisis centres. Nationally 9+1 states ban all-government-building access; 4 states criminalise in circumstances. Universal exposure for any outed visitor using public facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Bans mostly government-owned; 29 states plus capital have none. Trespass statutes elsewhere require refusal-to-depart, not automatic arrest.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal building rules and state orders align; no pre-emption conflict to shelter the traveller.

care_services.exposure: SB 904 (signed 14 May 2026) bars public funds, Medicaid and state facilities from gender-affirming care for minors AND adults; provider violations a misdemeanour. Visitor relying on public/Medicaid-adjacent care is exposed. National EO attacks youth care; subpoenas of under-19 records.
care_services.protection: Emergency treatment to prevent death or major impairment exempt; private facilities with private insurance/out-of-pocket remain available; mental-health and several medications exempt.
care_services.interaction: Emergency exemption limits but does not remove denial-of-care risk for routine or post-incident treatment.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; Dec 2025 reward memo references 'radical gender ideology' among extremist animating viewpoints; Jan 2025 order directs investigation of 'gender ideology' in schools. 66% of poll respondents support sex-at-birth document laws.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Dossier states reward criterion is not gender ideology and counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; comparison to genocide stages is advocacy framing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Institutional hostility raises the temperature on routine document and facility encounters.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling family faces K-12 facility bans, 27-state youth care bans, sports bans, no-promo-homo and diversity-training bans in this state; Jan 2025 order threatens criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; national health rules would bar under-18 coverage.
minors_guardians.protection: Existed care carve-outs (emergency, mental health); national employment and hate-crime protections; litigation pending on several orders.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent's and child's exposures compound: school exclusion plus care denial plus possible state inquiry.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2018 death threats against a 12-year-old trans student; Nex Benedict 2024 case (resident). State hate-crime law omits gender identity; only 23 states cover it; 22 states plus capital outlaw GI discrimination — this state does not. 2025 arrest of a trans student in a neighbouring capitol restroom.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers GI and is prosecutable federally; no state-specific violence against a visitor documented; no trans-specific killings documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin local recourse means a visitor assaulted here depends on federal prosecution and local police willingness.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state discrimination protection; at-will employment; marker-change litigation losing (Oct 2026 state supreme court ruling). HB 1225 status unresolved; passport litigation unresolved; visitor risk grade not stated.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts have enjoined several federal orders; national employment ruling and hate-crime statute operate; advocacy legal aid active.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slower and thinner here than the national average, but not illusory.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far worse than 0.15-B: no documented routine detention of trans visitors here, no custodial assaults as standard practice for visitors, no capital penalty plausibly linked to identity, habeas/courts function and have granted injunctions. Entry scrutiny and facility/care exclusion are serious but do not approach months-long cells with impunity.

Closest analogue: routine document/checkpoint exposure, indefinite verification, documented detention and denial of care, narrow anti-discrimination claims, inconsistent enforcement, scarce remedies. This dossier adds a stronger state hostile layer (adult care ban, facility order) but retains functioning federal courts and hate-crime coverage, so similar, marginally below or level.

Materially safer than 0.85-B: that anchor has border recognition of trans documents, specialist training, legal aid at detention, no expression criminalisation with working tribunal remedies. Here marker restriction is in force, entry cable mandates refusals, and the state adds facility and adult-care bans with no state-level protections.

Safer than 0.25-E: that anchor documents birth-sex shelter placement plus police-licensed raids with extortion and stalled commission remedies. Here facility exposure exists but no documented raids, shakedowns or bribery pattern against visitors; remedies, though uneven, function in federal courts.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: a national document/entry regime that treats marker mismatch as possible fraud (refusal, possible lifetime ineligibility, documented stranding and foreign advisories) layered over a state that independently restricts facilities (schools plus a blanket 2023 order covering shelters and incarceration), forecloses marker changes, and bars public-facility and publicly funded gender-affirming care for adults as well as minors. Outed exposure is therefore continuous — entry, facilities, care, and any custody encounter — but consequences stop short of imprisonment for status itself: emergency care is exempt, private care remains available, no trans-specific criminal offence applies, federal courts function and have enjoined orders, and national hate-crime and employment protections operate. State-level recourse is thin (no discrimination or GI hate-crime coverage), so severity sits at major friction, exclusion and possible entry refusal rather than custody — an Elevated Risk reading below the anchors showing administrative exclusion without remedy, above those where detention or extortion is routine.
